newsitem.title: PAPUA NEW GUINEA: PNG accuses Australia of character assassination.
newsitem.headline: PNG accuses Australia of character assassination.

text.p: Papua New Guinea Prime Minister Bill Skate has charged Australia with character assassination of South Pacific ministers after the release of a report critical of the island nations, a newspaper said on Friday.

Skate said the South Pacific would find it hard to understand a document which called one minister a "lickspittle" sidekick, another "Mister Ten Percent" and charged others with sending their nations bankrupt through economic mismanagement.

"It is quite unfortunate...a close friend and important and active player in the region could make such an assessment of how countries in the region have been managing their affairs, and to assassinate the character of selected leaders," Skate said.

"Australia has to appreciate it is part of the South Pacific region and the kind of attitude portrayed in the report makes it difficult for the other island nations to comprehend," Skate told The National newspaper.
Skate dismissed Australian comments that the report was merely a briefing paper and not government policy.

"Whilst it is alleged the information in the report is not the official position of the federal (Australian) government, it clearly gives new perception of how they view the relationship between Australia and the rest of the South Pacific," he said.
Other South Pacific nations, such as Nauru and the Cook Islands, have said the report will damage Australia's relations with the region.
The 93-page secret document was prepared as a briefing for Australian Treasurer Peter Costello ahead of a summit of economic ministers from the 16-member South Pacific Forum earlier this month.
The document was left on a table in a public area at the economic ministers' meeting, where it was obtained by Reuters.
